ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against: (i) FINTRAC PCMLTFA reportable-transaction standards; (ii) Criminal Code (Canada) terrorist entity lists; (iii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) country-based lists; (v) OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions lists; and (vi) domestic Alberta Securities Commission cease-trade files. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies because payment rails include cryptocurrency (USDC); the entity must adopt a written risk-based AML/CFT program, verify source of cryptocurrency funds, and report suspicious transactions to FINTRAC in accordance with PCMLTFA s. 7.1 and regulations respecting virtual currency dealing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry – CORES (Corporate Registry Electronic System) accessed through an accredited service provider portal; official gateway: https://www.albertacorporateaccess.gov.ab.ca; NUANS name search conducted via a licensed NUANS search house
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Legal name must be expressed in English or French using the Latin alphabet; foreign-script words (e.g., Chinese characters) are not permitted in the registered corporate name and must be transliterated into pinyin; the name must include the mandatory designator 'Unlimited Liability Company' or the abbreviation 'ULC' per the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, s. 13(1)
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting government authority or professional regulator affiliation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name may be renewed once for an additional 90 days through the accredited CORES service provider before expiry. If the Registrar refuses a proposed name, the applicant must obtain written reasons, then either (i) submit a revised name via the same CORES channel, or (ii) file a formal reconsideration request with the Registrar of Corporations within 30 days of refusal; if reconsideration is denied, judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta may be commenced within the applicable limitation period. In all cases, statutory fees are non-refundable and the appeal does not suspend the 90-day reservation clock.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only as a registered-office service where a physical Alberta street address is maintained by a licensed corporate agent and process can be served during normal business hours; pure virtual or mail-forwarding-only addresses without a physical presence are not acceptable for an Alberta ULC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45%–60% probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 36 months of operation, driven by the public web-scraping/API commercial model combined with USDC cryptocurrency payment exposure; inspection triggers include FINTRAC examination powers under PCMLTFA, CRA GST/HST and income tax field audits, and Alberta Corporate Registry compliance reviews.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9; incorporation provisions ss. 8-26; Unlimited Liability Corporation provisions Part 17.1, ss. 211.01-211.4
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed under s. 8 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital. An Alberta ULC may issue shares for such consideration as the directors may determine; no statutory escrow or capital deposit account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The incorporation subscription is accepted for 100 Class A common shares at CAD 1.00 per share by the founding shareholder, payment to be made upon demand of the board. (2) The company's registered office shall be established at the address stated in the Certificate of Incorporation; the Corporate Secretary is instructed to file the notice of office change and make all requisite registry updates. (3) The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until a successor is appointed. (4) The directors are authorized to execute all documents and take all steps required to complete statutory incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry - Registry Xpress; Service Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search for the proposed corporate name through the Registry Xpress online portal. If a name is requested, reserve it before incorporation; otherwise, use a numbered company designation assigned by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Certificate (if a name is requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, submit a fresh NUANS search and alternate name through Registry Xpress; reconsideration may be requested from the Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Execute, and Acknowledge Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator or legal counsel; submission via Alberta Corporate Registry - Registry Xpress
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute the Articles of Incorporation, setting forth the corporate name, registered office address, authorized share structure, directors, and any restrictions. In online filing, notarization is not typically required; each incorporator signs and each named director executes a consent to act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, correct the stated defect and refile within the regulatory response period; additional filing fees may apply upon resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry (Registry Xpress)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Articles of Incorporation package and pay the applicable corporate registry filing fee. Upon review and approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which establishes the legal existence and incorporation date of the ULC.
required_dossiers: NUANS report or numbered company confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, submit amended Articles of Incorporation with cured deficiencies; if the certificate is lost, request a duplicate Certificate of Status from the Alberta Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Board Resolution and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Alberta ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pass the first board resolution approving share subscriptions, adopting the registered office, appointing officers, approving the corporate seal if adopted, and authorizing opening of bank accounts and further administrative steps. This may be done by unanimous written consent in lieu of a physical meeting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect is identified in the organizational documents, adopt a corrective unanimous board resolution and, if necessary, file Articles of Amendment with the Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations and Statutory Minute Book Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC with the Canada Revenue Agency through Business Registration Online to obtain the Business Number, corporate income tax account, and GST/HST account where applicable. Complete the Alberta corporate tax account registration if required and establish the statutory minute book maintaining registers, resolutions, and share records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or provincial registration is delayed, contact the appropriate helpline and file a late registration; penalties may be remitted under the CRA taxpayer relief provisions for reasonable delay.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - office-based software/data services under ISIC 6201 do not require an industrial manufacturing license in Alberta

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical plant, manufacturing process, emissions source, or discharge point; Class B office occupancy only
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous air emissions generated; however, the office premises must comply with applicable municipal waste disposal, recycling, and sanitation bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office leasehold requires fire safety compliance, building code occupancy inspection, and occupational health and safety clearance under the Alberta Safety Codes Act and the Occupational Health and Safety Act, including certified fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and workplace hazard assessment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; online portal: CRA Business Registration Online and CRA My Business Account at canada.ca; Alberta incorporation portal: Alberta Corporate Registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation through the Alberta Corporate Registry; there is no minimum capital requirement and non-resident ownership is permitted. Step 2: Apply for a Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online or by filing Form RC1, Request for a Business Number and Program Accounts. Step 3: The BN is the statutory Canadian tax identifier; it will normally be assigned with RT (GST/HST) and TP (corporate income tax) program accounts. Step 4: The AB ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation and must file T2 corporate income tax returns; if taxable supplies made in Canada exceed the small-supplier threshold, it must register, collect, and remit GST/HST using the RT account. Step 5: For foreign owners, no separate Canadian TIN is required; foreign ownership is disclosed on the T2 return and dividend payments may be subject to Canadian withholding tax. The commercial web scraping and proxy API gateway business requires no additional national tax or statutory licence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible for U.S. federal check-the-box purposes; however, for Canadian income tax purposes the AB ULC is an entity-level taxpayer, i.e. a taxable Canadian corporation, not a partnership or disregarded entity. Canada applies residence-based worldwide taxation, and the ULC's unlimited liability and non-resident ownership do not create CRA-recognised tax transparency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic check-the-box election. The AB ULC may elect for U.S. federal tax classification under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3 by filing IRS Form 8832 to be treated as a corporation, partnership, or disregarded entity; a single-member ULC may become disregarded for U.S. tax while remaining a Canadian taxpayer. No Canadian hybrid mismatch election is available; CRA applies the general anti-avoidance rule and treaty anti-avoidance principles where hybrid arrangements are used. Under GST/HST there is no election to override the place-of-supply rules, although voluntary registration is permitted for small suppliers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax; Alberta has no provincial sales tax or PST component)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; GST/HST registration is generally mandatory for a business whose total taxable supplies made in Canada, calculated in the current and immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters, exceed CAD 30,000. A non-resident may also register voluntarily; once registered, GST at 5% applies to taxable supplies made in Canada unless the supply is zero-rated or exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable as a real-time fiscal clearance regime: Canada does not require government invoice stamping, a clearance API, or mandatory e-invoicing for GST/HST. Invoices may be kept electronically under section 286 of the Excise Tax Act; the PEPPOL e-invoice network is voluntary. GST/HST returns are transmitted electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or certified tax preparation software, with no invoice-level API approval. The enterprise should maintain audit-proof transactional records for Stripe and cryptocurrency payment rails, including ledger records, foreign client identifiers, and zero-rating evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A commercial scraping / proxy API service supplied to a non-resident customer is eligible for 0% GST if the supply is a service made to a non-resident person under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act and the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed. Data and API services delivered over the internet to foreign clients are generally zero-rated even if the service provider's servers are in Canada. Goods exported from Canada are zero-rated if sold to a non-resident and exported as soon as feasibly possible. The AB ULC may claim input tax credits and, where applicable, refunds for GST paid on Canadian inputs attributable to zero-rated exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Executed API subscription or SaaS agreement identifying the non-resident customer and describing the data/API service supplied
Commercial invoices on ULC letterhead showing the CRA Business Number, the words zero-rated export, and no GST charged
Evidence of non-resident status of the customer, such as foreign registration, foreign tax identification number, registered foreign address, and confirmation of no permanent establishment in Canada
Payment evidence: bank inward remittance, SWIFT confirmation, Stripe payout statement, or cryptocurrency transaction hash and conversion record
Delivery and usage logs evidencing API access and data destination endpoints outside Canada
Where physical goods are involved, a Canada Border Services Agency export declaration or B13A and a bill of lading
Where applicable, an inward remittance certificate or equivalent bank statement supporting satisfaction of the 180-day repatriation control
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess export zero-rating within the normal four-year reassessment period or later in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. If the exporter cannot substantiate a supply to a non-resident, or the commercial scraping API is found to be supplied for Canadian consumption, CRA can claw back the 0% rate and assess 5% GST on the full consideration, deny associated input tax credits, and charge daily compound interest. Gross-negligence and false-statement penalties may apply under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act, and deliberate evasion is prosecutable under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act. Transfer-pricing and general anti-avoidance rules may reattribute income to the Canadian ULC where artificial offshore invoicing is used. The 180-day payment parameter is a compliance pipeline documentation control and does not override the substantive CRA evidentiary requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority, together with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential bank regulation and the Department of Finance Canada for exchange-rate and international financial policy coordination.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada accepts IMF Article VIII obligations and maintains full convertibility for both current account and capital account transactions. The Canadian dollar is free-floating and there are no exchange-control restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or capital repatriation. Cross-border remittances remain subject to Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (generally 25% absent a treaty, with appropriate treaty relief available), plus FINTRAC reporting for electronic funds transfers at or above CAD 10,000. CRS, FATCA, and AML/KYC requirements must be satisfied by the receiving bank, but there are no currency convertibility or registration hurdles for ordinary trade or investment flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not impose any export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion timeline, or minimum conversion ratio. Exporters may invoice in any currency, retain revenue in permitted foreign-currency accounts with an authorized financial institution, and convert to CAD at market rates. There is no statutory deadline for repatriation of export receipts. Reporting obligations are limited to general anti-money-laundering declarations (FINTRAC EFT reports for CAD 10,000 or above) and the usual CRA corporate income and foreign-asset reporting thresholds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium as a supplementary collection tool, Low as a primary banking rail. Foreign electronic-money institutions and fintech EMI platforms are not banks in Canada and cannot accept retail deposits except through an OSFI-regulated institution. An offshore EMI can be used for low-value receivable aggregation and FX conversion only where settlement balances remain in a Canadian Schedule I bank, the EMI is registered with FINTRAC as a money-services business or operates under a valid provincial MSB licence, and the platform can evidence sanctions screening and transaction audit trails. The Alberta ULC must not leave operational liquidity stored on a passive EMI ledger; all net funds must circulate through the principal Canadian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act does not compel a physical appearance of directors; identity verification can be performed through reliable documentary methods and video. In practice, major Canadian banks impose enhanced due diligence on an Alberta ULC with non-resident shareholders, unlimited liability, and web-scraping/cryptocurrency payment flows, so the onboarding committee will usually require a live video interview with the directors, notarized or certified copies of passports and proofs of address, and an Alberta corporate registry profile that shows the authorized signatories. Remote account opening is available at most Schedule I banks, but some banks will nevertheless require at least one authorized signatory to visit an Alberta branch or a Canadian embassy/consulate to execute documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership of an unlimited-liability company used as a treasury vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta certificate of incorporation and standing search; certificate of unlimited-liability status; register of directors and shareholders; 25%-threshold beneficial-ownership schedule; notarized passport and address documentation; bank reference from the parent company; corporate resolutions appointing bank signatories; source-of-funds statements for the proposed initial deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume API/web-scraping receipts combined with USDC crypto settlement, creating opaque or unexplained revenue streams.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial contracts and end-user license agreements; accredited customer onboarding policy; privacy impact assessment and PIPEDA/GDPR counsel opinion; data collection and deletion logs; sanctions and adverse-media screening reports; wallet and blockchain analytics for USDC flows; USDC-to-CAD conversion records through a FINTRAC-registered MSB or regulated VASP; audited revenue reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent intercompany funding and capital-escrow movements without demonstrable economic activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organizational chart; executed intercompany loan or subscription agreements; transfer-pricing documentation under OECD guidelines; board minutes authorizing capital injection and treasury operations; six-month cash-flow forecast; invoices and service delivery records; payroll or contractor proof for the Alberta employees; CRA business number and tax return acknowledgements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder advances must be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 from the investor’s bank to the ULC’s operational or capital-escrow account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. The payment message should include the investor legal name, the ULC beneficiary name and account number, and a clear corporate-purpose reference such as 'ULC capital contribution / share subscription.' The receiving bank will require a board resolution, subscription agreement, share register update, and source-of-funds proof; wire values of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable to FINTRAC. If the investor originates in USDC/crypto, funds must first be passed through a FINTRAC-registered exchange or licensed MSB that converts to CAD, or be received by the bank-approved VASP corridor; direct on-chain transfer to the bank account is generally not permissible.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For external vendors, suppliers, and licensing partners, use SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for cross-border fiat settlements; use MT700/SWIFT commercial letters of credit only when underlying merchandise transactions require presentation of shipping and compliance documents. For CAD disbursements within Canada, settle via LVTS or EFT to an operational account with automated positive pay reconciliation using invoice references. USD payments from Canada may be cleared through CHIPS, Fedwire, or the Canadian bank’s US-dollar clearing network. USDC can be used only where the counterparty has an explicit treasury acceptance and the conversion or disbursement occurs via an OSFI-supervised bank or registered MSB, never from the operational account without a documented treasury policy and tax trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD FX forwards under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
CAD/EUR and CAD/GBP plain-vanilla FX forwards with a licensed Canadian Schedule I bank
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) for term-locking capital and trade-flow conversions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies that are not freely deliverable in Canada, transacted only with an OSFI-authorized derivative counterparty
FX options (purchased and covered written) for hedging, subject to board-approved treasury risk limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act (Alberta), s.126)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary date; fixed anniversary cycle, not linked to fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty CAD 50 added to the CAD 50 base fee; directors and officers liable on summary conviction to a fine up to CAD 5,000; Registrar may administratively strike off or dissolve the ULC after two consecutive years of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (December 31 year-end means June 30 filing deadline)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeat failure triggers 10% plus 2% per month; compounded daily arrears interest applies; directors may face personal liability for unremitted withholdings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta AT1 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end, mirroring the federal T2 filing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid provincial tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; prescribed interest accrues on unpaid amounts; TRA may place a compliance hold affecting the corporation's registry standing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory records; available for inspection by the Alberta Corporate Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Rolling obligation; update within 15 days of any ISC change and re-certify annually alongside the Alberta Annual Return at anniversary plus 60 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence-based fines up to CAD 200,000 and/or imprisonment for knowingly failing to prepare, maintain, or provide the ISC register; directors authorizing non-compliance face personal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (federal 5% GST; Alberta has no provincial sales tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers with taxable revenue not exceeding CAD 1.5 million file within 3 months after fiscal year-end; quarterly and monthly filers file within 1 month after each reporting period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Excise Tax Act penalty of 5% of net unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; culpable conduct penalty up to 50% of understated tax; prescribed arrears interest compounded daily

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit threshold for a private Alberta ULC; audit exemption applies unless shareholders holding at least 5% of issued shares demand an audit (ABCA s.160) or a unanimous shareholder resolution requires one; distributing (public-offering) corporations must appoint a licensed public accountant. Private ULCs typically adopt a unanimous resolution waiving the auditor and audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) permitted for private ULCs; IFRS mandatory for distributing corporations; tax accounting must track capital cost allowance on Class 50 (computer hardware) and Class 12 (software), accrued API subscription revenue, foreign exchange gains on USDC holdings, and intercompany USD/CAD settlements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta ABCA transparency rules require the ULC to maintain an ISC register identifying every individual with significant control (threshold of 25% or more of shares or voting rights, or de facto control); entries record name, residential address, control date, and nature of control; the register must be updated within 15 days of any change and re-certified annually at the Annual Return filing; annual confirmation is signed by a director and re-verified upon any share transfer, including transfers to non-resident U.S. shareholders of this pass-through-eligible ULC.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 185-740 per year (CAD 250-1,000) for registered office and corporate agent services in Calgary or Edmonton; most mandates include annual return preparation and filing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,600-11,100 (CAD 3,500-15,000) for a full statutory audit by a CPA firm; USD 1,100-3,700 (CAD 1,500-5,000) for a review engagement or notice-to-reader where a shareholder waiver is available
